Load packages:
```{r}
library(data.table)
```

Exemple data:
```{r}
DT <- data.table(
  id = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3),
  var = c(10, 20, 15, 5, 8, 12)
)

DT[, max_var := max(var), by = id]
```

# SAS DATA STEP: SELECT GROUP

``` sas
data DT;
    set DT;

    select;
        when (var = 10) gruppo = "A";
        when (var = 20) gruppo = "B";
        when (var = 15) gruppo = "C";
        otherwise gruppo = "ALTRO";
    end;
run;
```

## `data.table` equivalent with `fcase()`

```{r}
DT[, gruppo := fcase(
  var == 10, "A",
  var == 20, "B",
  var == 15, "C",
  default = "OTHER"
)]

DT
```

`fcase()` evaluates the conditions in sequence and returns the value associated with the first condition that evaluates to true.

## Recode two or more variables

SAS code

``` sas
select;
    when (var < 10) classe = 1;
    when (var >= 10 and var < 20) classe = 2;
    when (var >= 20) classe = 3;
    otherwise classe = 0;
end;
```

`data.table` code

```{r}
DT[, classe := fcase(
  var < 10, 1L,
  var >= 10 & var < 20, 2L,
  var >= 20, 3L,
  default = 0L
)]

DT
```

# SAS DATA STEP: if-then-else

To create `dummies` use this function (`fifelse`):

```{r}
DT[, classe := fifelse(var > 10, "A", "B")]

DT
```

`fifelse()` is the equivalent of an IF-THEN-ELSE, whilst fcase() is particularly well suited to replicating SELECT-WHEN-OTHERWISE.

For the migration from SAS to R/data.table, use `fcase()` to translate the SELECT-WHEN blocks.

# SAS IF-THEN DO; ... END; ELSE DO; ... END;

To translate a SAS block such as IF-THEN DO; ... END; ELSE DO; ... END; into a data.table, it depends on what you need to do: assign variables or execute multiple statements.

## SAS: IF-THEN-ELSE with more assignments:

``` sas
data want;
    set have;
    if var > 10 then do;
        classe = "A";
        flag = 1;
        valore = var * 2;
    end;
    else do;
        classe = "B";
        flag = 0;
        valore = var;
    end;
run;
```

`data.table`: multiple assignments using `:=` This is probably the most natural way to write code when working with 
`data.table`.

```{r}
DT[var > 10, `:=`(
  classe = "A",
  flag = 1L,
  valore = var * 2
)]

DT[var <= 10, `:=`(
  classe = "B",
  flag = 0L,
  valore = var
)]

DT
```

## Correspondence SAS → `data.table`

| SAS DATA STEP                   | data.table                |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------------|
| `if condition then`             | `DT[condition, ...]`      |
| `else`                          | `DT[!condition, ...]`     |
| `do; ... end;`                  | `.(...)` oppure `{ ... }` |
| `x = value;`                    | `x := value`              |
| `if-then-else` su una variabile | `fifelse()`               |
| `select-when`                   | `fcase()`                 |
